judgment.notes: T,gamma,R are real, with exactly T>0, 0<gamma<=1 and R>0. The only declared roots are H001–H003 and E001–E006. Following every helper's inputs preserves the original direct boundaries; T013 is unconditional weighted-Sobolev infrastructure, not a new hypothesis, and no background note is promoted. E002 retains -1<theta<=0, constants before the horizon, the L2 norm-sum condition and both unitary versions. E004 retains every beta endpoint, the admissible positive-epsilon threshold, mean-zero inputs, n>=0 and uniformity; E005 retains sigma=0 and both epsilon endpoints; E006 copies the full unfiltered identity. However E003 is a stronger external assumption than its source: XPath uses Weak, whose analytic compactly supported test functions are all zero, so its derivative arguments need not be weak derivatives at all. The imported bound thus applies to additional paths and independently chosen derivative norms. E001 also imports SourceApprox through the time-analytic SmoothOn predicate, beyond the source's smooth-approximation clause. The endpoint_correspondence claims do not establish these equivalences.

The Fourier model otherwise has the specified integer frequencies, complex coefficients, even positive weights, guarded summability, conjugate symmetry and zero mode. FromLP uses the invertible weight (1+k²)^(-s/2); pinned lp has exponent p:ℝ≥0∞, so lp ... 2 is genuinely square-summable, and T013 explicitly obligates both realization directions, norm equality, truncation density, inclusions and completeness. The signs of S, B and sourceB, reflection, inverse derivatives, convolution and all four Htau terms agree with their source objects. The n2/n3 pairwise formulas give the second/third largest magnitudes, including ties; thresholds are real and grid indices natural. EssBound guards finiteness before ENNReal.toReal, and continuous-path guards justify real suprema. But pinned ContDiff/ContDiffOn take an order in WithTop ℕ∞: their outer top is analytic order ω, distinct from smooth order. Header Weak uses ContDiff ℝ ⊤ for its tests, making the testing condition trivial by analytic uniqueness on ℝ. SmoothOn uses ContDiffOn ℝ ⊤ and therefore strengthens C∞ paths to time-analytic coefficients. Smooth-to-analytic and arbitrary-derivative-to-weak-derivative reverse conversions are invalid. No weighted-lp, density or type-elaboration obligation fixes either mismatch.
